findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — The link lightness pair is reversed; use `$primary` 30% for light themes and `$secondary` 70% for dark themes to avoid low-contrast text.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` reverses the intended lightness values; preserve `$primary` 70% and use `$secondary` 30% to match the desktop rule.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `a.star h3` incorrectly uses 50% lightness in both themes; preserve 20% for light themes and use the complementary 80% for dark themes to maintain contrast from the adjacent `h4`.
app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` incorrectly changes from `$primary` 30% to a 50%/50% pair; preserve `$primary` 30% and use `$secondary` 70%.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` incorrectly changes from `$primary` 30% to a 50%/50% pair, reducing contrast; use `$primary` 30% and `$secondary` 70%.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` reverses the intended lightness values; preserve `$primary` 70% and use `$secondary` 30% to match the desktop rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an inconsistency. Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. However, the desktop version in desktop/modal.scss line 50 changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The mobile version has the values reversed (30%/70% instead of 70%/30%), which appears to be an error since the original value was 70% for $primary in both files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `a.star h3` incorrectly uses 50% lightness in both themes; preserve 20% for light themes and use the complementary 80% for dark themes to maintain contrast from the adjacent `h4`.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, the h3 element was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the lightness from 20% to 50% for light themes, which is inconsistent with other h3 elements in the codebase (e.g., desktop/topic-post.scss line 321 uses 20%/80%). The adjacent h4 at line 190 uses 50%/50%, so using the same values for h3 would reduce the visual hierarchy/contrast between h3 and h4. This appears to be an unintentional change that breaks the design consistency.
